claims.metric: predictive log-likelihood and RMSE improvement vs state-of-the-art
claims.quote: We show a considerable improvement in predictive log-likelihood and RMSE compared to existing state-of-the-art methods

conditions.comparison: different model architectures and non-linearities in regression

claims.quote: We compare the uncertainty obtained from different model architectures and non-linearities in regression, and show that model uncertainty is indispensable for classification tasks, using MNIST as a concrete example.

claims.metric: predictive log-likelihood and RMSE improvement via dropout uncertainty
claims.quote: We then show that using dropout's uncertainty we can obtain a considerable improvement in predictive log-likelihood and RMSE compared to existing state-of-the-art methods.

claims.metric: significant improvement in RMSE and uncertainty estimation vs baselines
claims.quote: In the results section we compare dropout to these approaches and show a significant improvement in both RMSE and uncertainty estimation.

claims.metric: GP predictive uncertainty on extrapolation point

conditions.model: Gaussian process with squared exponential covariance function

claims.quote: The GP model represents this by increasing its predictive uncertainty – in effect declaring that the predictive value might be 0 but the model is uncertain.

claims.metric: MC dropout captures GP-like uncertainty behavior

conditions.model: same 5-layer ReLU as Fig 2a, MC dropout for predictive mean and uncertainty

claims.quote: This behaviour is captured in MC dropout as well.

conditions.plot: predictive mean ± 2 standard deviations (95% confidence), each colour gradient = 0.5 std dev, plotted with 8× std dev for visualization

claims.quote: Fig. 2d shows the same using the TanH network with 5 layers (plotted with 8 times the standard deviation for visualisation purposes). The shades of blue represent model uncertainty: each colour gradient represents half a standard deviation (in total, predictive mean plus/minus 2 standard deviations are shown, representing 95% confidence).

claims.metric: MC dropout expresses uncertainty via increased std dev despite incorrect mean

conditions.uncertainty: increased standard deviation expresses model uncertainty

claims.quote: Even though the models in figures 2 have an incorrect predictive mean, the increased standard deviation expresses the models' uncertainty about the point.

claims.metric: uncertainty trend far from data: ReLU vs TanH

conditions.explanation: ReLU and TanH approximate different GP covariance functions; TanH saturates, ReLU does not

claims.quote: Note that the uncertainty is increasing far from the data for the ReLU model, whereas for the TanH model it stays bounded.

claims.metric: dropout probability 0.1 vs 0.2 convergence for TanH

conditions.initial: p=0.1 exhibits smaller uncertainty than p=0.2

claims.quote: Models initialised with dropout probability 0.1 initially exhibit smaller uncertainty than the ones initialised with dropout probability 0.2, but towards the end of the optimisation when the model has converged the uncertainty is almost indistinguishable.

claims.metric: dropout model moments convergence to GP moments
claims.quote: It seems that the moments of the dropout models converge to the moments of the approximated GP model – its mean and uncertainty.

conditions.attempt: fit data with models with smaller number of layers

claims.quote: It is worth mentioning that we attempted to fit the data with models with a smaller number of layers unsuccessfully.

conditions.outputs: softmax input (last FC layer) and softmax output for top classes

claims.quote: For the 12 images, the model predicts classes [1 1 1 1 1 5 5 7 7 7 7 7].

claims.metric: uncertainty envelope separation implies high confidence

conditions.condition: uncertainty envelope of a class far from others

claims.quote: Looking at the softmax input values, if the uncertainty envelope of a class is far from that of other classes' (for example the left most image) then the input is classified with high confidence.

claims.metric: uncertainty envelope intersection implies high prediction uncertainty
claims.quote: On the other hand, if the uncertainty envelope intersects that of other classes (such as in the case of the middle input image), then even though the softmax output can be arbitrarily high (as far as 1 if the mean is far from the means of the other classes), the softmax output uncertainty can be as large as the entire space. This signifies the model's uncertainty in its softmax output value – i.e. in the prediction.

conditions.claim: forward passes can be done concurrently, resulting in constant running time identical to standard dropout

claims.quote: Furthermore, the forward passes can be done concurrently, resulting in constant running time identical to that of standard dropout.
